pool_preserving_layout_gate.reason: Literal pool calls remove padding but multiply launch/compile boundaries. Earlier exact variants with fewer boundaries were already 31--36% slower. The only viable design packs pool-local rows inside the existing outer calls using the shared compact-pair machinery.

decisions.evidence: Job 13260861 is bitwise exact in 15/15 sampled blocks and saves ~0.061 s per 200-row two-pass slice, only ~4.9 s over 80 iterations; the first clean full pair was 1.45% slower.
Jobs 13261042/13261159 are bitwise exact; job 13261339 crosses over near batch 45 and reaches only 1.01115x at batch 200. GF46 has one batch per pass, so its end-to-end ceiling is below 0.52%.

Exclusive same-H100 job 13260950 reduced median wall by 7.56%, but fail-closed operand job 13265965 found different iteration-1 artifacts before the two caps predict different topology. Commit 732868abb records that no causal x-half invariant was established; no split was implemented or promoted.

Job 13262146 proves exact source chronology and 49.5--82.2% fewer logical padded rows, but raises calls from 3--7 to 67--120; earlier exact, less fragmented variants regressed 31--36%. Pursue macro-packed rows inside unchanged outer calls instead.

Jobs 13266322/13266460 preserve active raw scores, dense scores, all six shared-posterior outputs, poisoned-tail no-op behavior, and outer-call cardinality bitwise. GF46 iteration-20/40/60/80 score-plus-posterior calls are 32.88%, 35.77%, 54.53%, and 32.68% lower, but projection/packing and trajectory costs are not measured.

decisions.status: NUMERICALLY EQUIVALENT; END-TO-END GAIN IMMATERIAL/INCONCLUSIVE; DEFAULT OFF
decisions.evidence: Primitive job 13269547 is bitwise exact at GF46 iterations 20/40/60/80 and 7.1839--31.6257x faster at the isolated warmed exponentiate-plus-divide boundary. Jobs 13269681/13271166 have zero particle-state and schedule escapes. The strict two-control map-diameter diagnostic flags roundoff-scale relative-L2 differences, but the same-binary rerun moves them to candidate repeat 2 at iterations 2/3 while all four arms use identical CUDA bytes, supporting control-scale numerical variability rather than a basin change. Same-binary warm gain is only 1.0091x, so there is no large reproducible end-to-end advantage and no promotion.

next_gate.current_action: Implement and microgate a default-off K=1 multistream scheduler around the accepted shared production coarse kernel. Preserve its texture math and canonical reduction; measure discrete changes against control/native repeat variability and require stable, unbiased, non-growing numerical noise, the same basin, no material final-quality loss, and a meaningful end-to-end gain before promotion.
next_gate.hypothesis: RECOVAR's production coarse kernel is already slightly faster per executed slot than native RELION, but six serial padded batches produce a 4.355 s coarse union versus RELION's 2.752 s union from 1000 per-particle launches over eight streams. Scheduling overlap, not different projector arithmetic, is the dominant measured gap.
next_gate.evidence_pattern: The same-H100 A/B/C/D factorial keeps all tracked discrete decisions exact. Cache-only improves cold wall 1.24% and warm wall 5.27% with a 0.365 GiB HWM cost, so it is retained for repeat and scale gates. Physical-order chunking is rejected after a 14.09% cold regression and flat warm wall; the combined arm is not a default after a 15.05% cold regression and 11.35% HWM increase.
next_gate.narrowed_boundary: Persistent raw caching is a modest retained candidate, physical-order chunking is rejected, and the large remaining opportunity is shared coarse execution topology. Stable-window and flat-row work remain default-off supporting lanes; no frozen score changes until a full release gate passes.
